h1:
Halal Travel in Thailand
Muslim-Friendly, Worry-Free Travel
intro: Thailand is a favorite destination for Muslim travelers from Malaysia, Indonesia, and the Middle East — halal food is easy to find, there are mosques and prayer rooms, and people are welcoming, especially in the south, which is a predominantly Muslim region with plenty of halal options. This article sums up how to find halal food, which cities are most convenient, where the prayer rooms are, and what's good to know.
quickAnswerHtml: Thailand is friendly to Muslim travelers. You can find halal food by looking for the green halal certification mark (certified by Thailand's Central Islamic body). The south (Hat Yai, Pattani, and the border provinces) is a Muslim region where halal is easiest to find, while Bangkok has several halal-food districts. Prayer rooms are available in large malls and airports, and many Muslim-friendly hotels provide the qibla direction and a prayer mat (ask before booking).

blocks.html: Thailand ranks among the destinations Muslim travelers choose most often, because halal food is available in cities and tourist areas, there are mosques and prayer rooms, and the culture is welcoming. The most convenient region is the south, with its dense Muslim communities and halal on every corner, while big cities like Bangkok also have plenty of halal districts and restaurants to choose from.

blocks.title: Eating halal with peace of mind

items.title: Look for the halal mark
items.text: Certified restaurants display the green halal certification mark (certified by Thailand's Central Islamic body). Look for it at the storefront or on the menu.

items.title: Ask "Is it halal?"
items.text: Just say the word "halal" — Thais understand it. Muslim-run restaurants or places with an Islamic food sign are a safe bet.

items.title: Use apps and maps
items.text: Halal restaurant-finder apps and maps make it easy to find nearby restaurants and mosques, especially in cities where halal spots are spread out.

items.title: Dishes that are usually halal
items.text: Khao mok gai (chicken biryani), mataba/murtabak, roti, beef soup, and southern Muslim-style dishes are easy to find at Islamic restaurants.

blocks.text: Cities and regions where halal is easy to find

items.name: The South (Hat Yai & the border provinces)
items.blurb: The Muslim region with the most halal — restaurants, mosques, and a familiar atmosphere. Hat Yai is a popular hub for Malaysian travelers.

items.name: Bangkok
items.blurb: Several halal districts and restaurants, including areas near mosques. The big malls have prayer rooms, and it's easy to get around.

items.name: Phuket & Krabi
items.blurb: Beach destinations with Muslim communities and halal restaurants scattered about — not hard to find in the tourist areas.

items.name: Chiang Mai
items.blurb: Has an old Muslim quarter in the heart of the city plus halal restaurants — great for anyone who wants to explore the north without worrying about food.

blocks.html: Prayer rooms are available in many large malls and at major airports (such as Suvarnabhumi), while mosques are found throughout cities and are especially dense in the south. As for where to stay, many Muslim-friendly hotels provide the qibla direction, a prayer mat, and a halal breakfast, particularly in the south and at international chains. We recommend confirming with the hotel before booking, and during Ramadan it's worth checking restaurants' opening and closing hours in advance.

faq.q: Is it easy to find halal food in Thailand?
faq.a: It's easy in the south and the big cities. Look for the green halal certification mark (certified by Thailand's Central Islamic body) at the storefront or on the menu, or just say the word "halal" when you ask. In the south — places like Hat Yai and the border provinces — halal is on every corner.

faq.q: Which city is best for Muslim travelers?
faq.a: The south (Hat Yai and the border provinces) is the Muslim region with the most halal and the most familiar feel. Bangkok, Phuket, Krabi, and Chiang Mai also have halal districts and restaurants to choose from.
Yes. Prayer rooms are available in many large malls and at major airports such as Suvarnabhumi, while mosques are found throughout cities and are especially dense in the south.

faq.q: Do hotels have facilities for Muslims?
faq.a: Many Muslim-friendly hotels provide the qibla direction, a prayer mat, and a halal breakfast, particularly in the south and at international chains. It's best to confirm with the hotel before booking.

faq.q: What does the halal mark look like?
faq.a: It's a green mark certified by Thailand's Central Islamic body, displayed at the storefront or on packaging. A restaurant with this mark has been certified as halal.
